Motion and presence data show when someb: Motion and presence data show when somebody is at home. Off by default.
Only states in a room or function: Only states in a room or function
Automatically selected states must belon: Automatically selected states must belong to a room or function (directly or by their channel or device). Include rules and per-state settings are not affected.
Events and keyframes older than this are: Events and keyframes older than this are deleted daily at 03:30
Changes are collected in memory and writ: Changes are collected in memory and written in one transaction. Longer intervals spare SD cards.
Patterns with * as wildcard, e.g. zigbee: Patterns with * as wildcard, e.g. zigbee.0.*.state. Include rules add states to the automatic selection, exclude rules remove them. Single states can also be set in the object browser (custom settings).
Excluded states are never recorded, even: Excluded states are never recorded, even if they match an include pattern
The preview shows which states would be: The preview shows which states would be recorded with the settings above, also before saving. The instance must be running.
Numbers are stored when they change by a: Numbers are stored when they change by at least the dead band, at most once per minimum interval (then the latest value), and changes within the dead band after the heartbeat. Defaults: temperature 0.2 / 60 s / 1 h, humidity 2 / 60 s / 1 h, brightness 10 % / 60 s / 1 h, dimmer and blind 1 / 0 s / none, power 5 % / 60 s / 15 min, other numbers 1 % / 60 s / 1 h. A rule below overrides the default of its roles; * is a wildcard (e.g. value.temperature*).
Changes per minute (average of an hour):: Changes per minute (average of an hour): such numbers are stored as 5 minute aggregates
Changes per minute: protects the databas: Changes per minute: protects the database from defective sensors. Other states above this average are not recorded. 0: off
Every change: no dead band, no throttlin: Every change: no dead band, no throttling, never aggregated automatically
Creates a read-only copy of every record: Creates a read-only copy of every recorded state under mirror.*. While replay.active is on, the replay writes the past values there: a vis view on the mirrors becomes a time machine.
While you are away, the simulation plays: While you are away, the simulation plays the switching of lights and blinds of a recorded day at home: the same weekday some weeks ago, shifted by a few minutes at random and by the sunset. Heating, locks, sockets, gates and read-only states are never switched. When you come back, it stops at once and switches off the lights it switched on.
Starts the simulation when it reports ab: Starts the simulation when it reports absence (e.g. 0_userdata.0.away or an armed alarm system) and stops it at once when it reports presence. Without a state, the simulation is switched with simulation.enabled.
The state reports presence (true = at ho: The state reports presence (true = at home)
The same weekday 1 to N weeks ago is cho: The same weekday 1 to N weeks ago is chosen at random; if none was at home, another day
Each group of switchings is shifted by u: Each group of switchings is shifted by up to this many minutes earlier or later
Afternoon and evening are shifted by the: Afternoon and evening are shifted by the difference of the sunsets (coordinates from the system settings)
Also switch media on and off: Also switch media on and off
Also play the switching of scripts: Also play the switching of scripts
Normally only the switching of persons i: Normally only the switching of persons is played (user interfaces, apps, switches on the wall), because scripts keep running anyway
